what: BeOne Medicines, formerly BeiGene, develops cancer medicines. Its main product Brukinsa treats blood cancers and competes directly with the established leaders in that class; it also sells an immunotherapy and other oncology treatments.
customers: Hospitals, oncologists and health systems in the United States, Europe and China.
money: BTK inhibitor for chronic lymphocytic leukaemia and other blood cancers
moat: Clinical trial data showing its lead medicine performs better than the established competitor in a head-to-head study, which is rare and hard to argue with.
risks: Most revenue comes from one medicine
Its China heritage has created political scrutiny in the United States
Competitors are developing next-generation medicines in the same class
Operating margin of 8% is thin while it funds a large research programme
opportunities: Revenue grew about 40% last year and about 56% a year over three years
It turned profitable, which few companies of this kind manage
Cash of about $6 billion against $1 billion of debt funds the pipeline
watch: Brukinsa market share against its main competitor, and pipeline trial results.
